problem: If $u=[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 6 \\ -2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ and $v=[\begin{aligned}k \\ 2 \\ -7 \\ 5\end{aligned}]$ are orthogonal vectors, then $k=$
worked_solution:
Since $u$ and $v$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that their dot product is equal to zero.
First, let's calculate the dot product in terms of $k$:

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & ={u}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {v}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {v}_{4} \\  & =(-8)\cdot k+6\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot (-7)+(-2)\cdot 5 \\  & =-8k+12+14-10 \\  & =-8k+16\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the dot product to zero, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-8k+16 & =0 \\ 8k & =16 \\ k & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
